answer: Because the sonnet ledger attributes every share, the horizon audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 69% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and hence it pays the violet fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 30 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
